reason: The CIF parses and round-trips as 32 fully occupied atoms (Cu8Hg4Sn4S16, reduced Cu2SnHgS4) in a cubic 10.5087 A cell and symmetry-recovers F-43m; primitive standardization gives one formula unit, and the trace provides strong 27-line indexing plus an auditable integrated-intensity fit. However, the instantiated topology fails the required periodic chemistry: the Cu 4d orbit (half of all Cu) has no S closer than 4.343 A and the entire Sn 4b orbit has no S closer than 4.372 A (both first S shells are 12-fold), whereas only Cu 4a and Hg 4c have plausible tetrahedral S shells at 2.194 and 2.357 A. Complete neighbor shells therefore confirm chemically isolated Cu and Sn sublattices, not a cutoff artifact. The trace itself rejected this same 32-atom F-43m topology for that defect before later resubmitting it; its intensity residual cannot rescue the chemically invalid realization, so another attempt is needed to instantiate a connected structure.
